main_text.p: nachifmi fructus blasphemiæ in doctrina hor-rendæ, & hæreses pene irradicabiles, tā est pertinax & rationi [illegible, ~7 letters] hoc hominum genus.) Hic igitur iā fenex sub Theodosio iuniore jam sene, quum Nestorium refutare vellet, & dogma de duabus in Christo personis revellere, dixit post unionem naturarum in Christo, non jam duas, sed unam tantum, nempe divinam naturam mansisse. Hoc quum publice profitere-tur, & inter suos monachos effutiret, deprehendit esse erroneū Eusebius Dorylæus episcopus (est autem Dorylum civitas Phrygiæ, ut ait Plinius lib.5.cap.29.) qui & Nestorii primus detexerat. Itaque res tota ad Flavianum tunc urbis Constantinopolitanæ episcopum delata est: sed quum non resipiscceret vetulus monachus, & senex obstinatus, Synodus provincialis a Flaviano Constantinopolin collecta est, in qua præsens, auditūsque Eutyches damnatur, & deponitur. De quo conquestus apud Theodosiū imperatorem, habuit Chrysaphium quendam inter cubicularios principis primarium sibi suoque errori fauentem, tum in odium Flaviani (oderat enim hypocrita & impius Chrysaphius pium hominem, & Dei servuum Flavianum) tum ruente jam Dei Ecclesia, & Satana (Domino Deo juste verbi sui contemptum, & tot jam in Oriente enatas hæreses vlcifcente) libere grassante etiā in media principis aula. Itaq; ut iterū Eutychis causa disceptaretur, convocata est Synodus Ephesum, quæ fuit secunda Ephesina Synodus, cui Flavianus interfuit: præfuit Diofcurus homo, si vllus alius, nequam, & ad omne scelus auda-

page.notes: The Greek word after "rationi" is not legible on the scan and is marked as illegible. Several spellings were normalised to the u/v and long-s rules; the printed text reads "Neftorium", "Chryfaphius" and "Ecclefia" with long s, and is given here with plain s. Some words could not be read with certainty (for example "fenex", "vlcifcente", "pium", "Dei servuum") and should be checked against the scan. The printed "Dorylum", "vnionem" and "fervuum" forms are copied as printed where the letters are clear; the word "Dei servuum Flavianum" reads as printed and may be a corrupted word in the original. The running head "Cap.92." is treated as the page number.
